name: unstructured
quote: Making good progress on the to-do list.
description: A pattern of being disorganized, undisciplined, somewhat scattered, and often late.
perceptions: There might be more to do.
I'll get to them when I get to them.

variations.name: messiness
variations.description: A pattern of keeping your mind, body, or environment poorly-ordered.
perceptions: Keeping things clean and neat is not worthwhile because they'll just get messy again soon enough.
results: Relatively disordered environment and/or personal appearance.

guidance.description: There are many sources that suggest a messy environment could indicate a mental health problem. This may be true, or it might not be. Here are some references that may be of interest.

commentaries.quote: The integral being is attached to nothing and can relate to everyone with an unstructured attitude. Because of this, her very existence benefits all things.
I would rather read a poorly structured story that has fresh ideas than a tightly structured one with cliches.
Perhaps it is better to be irresponsible and right, than to be responsible and wrong.
I'm super down with being irresponsible. I'm just trying to make sure my lack of responsibility no longer hurts people.
Being late is a way of saying that your own time is more valuable than the time of the person who waited for you.

Messiness ought to be celebrated. Instead, it’s a problem to solve, a bad habit to rectify, something to apologize for profusely when a visitor walks in. At best, you might forgive yourself or joke about your defect — your character flaw, really, since our culture associates messiness with laziness.
